newsitem.title: JORDAN: Banking gains lift Jordanian shares.
newsitem.headline: Banking gains lift Jordanian shares.

text.p: Strong gains in Jordanian banking stock on Monday helped push up shares on the Amman stock exchange by more than one percent.
Shrugging off a week-long fall, the official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 1.18 percent to 151.77 points in slim turnover of just 270,000 dinars ($381,000).

"There's an improvement in the banking stock, but there's no sign of a radical change in the market," said broker Husam Hanbali. Sunday's index closing level of 150.00 points was the lowest since late November.

Shares in the Housing Bank, which announced last week details of its plan to raise capital to 20 million dinars, rose 0.02 dinars to 4.72 dinars in trade worth 17,000 dinars, while Jordan National Bank maintained a recent recovery to pick up 0.04 dinars to 1.79 dinars.
But heavyweight Arab Bank, Monday's most busily traded share in terms of value, fell 0.50 dinars to 255.00 dinars after turnover of 56,000 dinars.
Overall gaining shares outnumbered losers by 22 to 14, with shares in another 12 companies trading but closing unchanged.
But the private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance fell 0.24 percent on Monday, down 5.37 percent since the start of the year.
